args.title: checkout-api: failed health checks after v2.3.1 deploy, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1, with error rate at 18%.

Remediation: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy production status. The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error, halted after us-east), leaving the fleet mixed: us-east on v2.3.0 and us-west/eu-west still on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout, and all three regions are now running v2.3.0.

Current status: Service is healthy; error rate is 0.002 (down from 0.18).

Notes: v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the cause of the health check failures is identified and fixed. The v2.3.1-rc build in staging is also marked unhealthy and may share the same defect.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions, unhealthy with a 18% error rate. Deployment history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent release with a healthy production status (v2.2.9 was also healthy but older; v2.3.1-rc is staging and also unhealthy).

**Action taken:** Rolled back to v2.3.0.
- First attempt **partially failed** — orchestrator error halted the rollout after us-east, leaving a mixed fleet (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1). I verified this via a status check rather than assuming success.
- Retried the rollback; it completed across all regions.

Since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production, this was a rollback rather than a deploy of an unproven version, so no change-manager approval was needed.

**Verified end state:** v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west; healthy: true; error rate 0.002.

**Incident:** Opened SEV2 INC-0001 for checkout-api, documenting the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback including the partial-failure detail, the recovered state, and a note that v2.3.1 shouldn't be redeployed until the health-check failure is understood (and that the v2.3.1-rc staging build may share the defect). The first create_incident call timed out, so I retried with the same idempotency key and confirmed via list_incidents that only one incident exists — the on-call engineer has been paged.

One thing worth flagging for follow-up: the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is still unknown, and the v2.3.1-rc staging build is also unhealthy — that's the likely next thread for whoever picks up the incident.

Rolling back to v2.3.0 — this version was previously healthy in production, so no change-manager approval is required.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The current version is v2.3.1, unhealthy. The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0 (seq 1).

Roll back to v2.3.0 in all production regions.

Note the policy: deploying a version that has never been healthy in production requires change-manager approval. v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, so rollback is fine.

Let me do the rollback, then create the incident. These are dependent in the sense that I should roll back first, then report. Actually I can state what I did. Better to roll back first, then create incident describing what I did.

Idempotency key for incident is optional but good practice.

transcript.content: The rollback partially failed — it halted during rollout. Let me check the current state before doing anything further.
transcript.reasoning_content: Partial failure. Need to check the status to see what happened.

transcript.content: The rollback left the fleet in a mixed state: us-east is on v2.3.0, while us-west and eu-west are still on the unhealthy v2.3.1. I'll retry the rollback to complete the remaining regions.
transcript.reasoning_content:
We're in a mixed state: us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1 (unhealthy). Need to retry the rollback to complete it. v2.3.0 is still healthy-in-production eligible, so no approval needed.

Let me retry the rollback.

transcript.content: The retry succeeded. Verifying health across regions.
transcript.reasoning_content: Now all regions on v2.3.0. Let me verify health.

transcript.content: All three regions are now on v2.3.0 and the service is healthy (error rate down from 18% to 0.2%). Opening the SEV2 incident.
